# School finances and closure: the early-warning model {#sec-finance-method}

```{r finance-method-setup}
#| include: false
FM <- readRDS(here::here("data", "finance_closures.rds"))   # written by R/43_finance_closures.R
FMm <- FM$model; FMt <- FM$test
fm_co <- as_tibble(FMm$coefs) |> rename(zc = z)
fm_eff <- as_tibble(FM$effects)
fm_term <- c(log_pupils = "log_pupils", chg3 = "chg3", util_c = "util_c", res = "res", iy = "iy", ipp = "ipp",
             area_primary_chg = "area_primary_chg", academy = "academyTRUE", secondary = "secondaryTRUE")
fm_tab <- fm_eff |> mutate(coef_term = fm_term[term]) |>
  left_join(fm_co, by = c("coef_term" = "term")) |>
  mutate(b_sd = est * sd, lo_sd = (est - 1.96 * se) * sd, hi_sd = (est + 1.96 * se) * sd)
fm_r2 <- 1 - FMm$dev / FMm$null_dev
fm_pc <- function(x, d = 0) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x)
fm_cut <- 100 * FM$now$cut[[1]]
```

[School finances before closure](finance.qmd) asks whether the schools that
closed looked different in the years before, and whether open schools look
like them now. This section sets out how that is done: what is predicted,
from what, by which model, how it was tested, and how its scores become the
counts published on the finance and area pages. The code is
`R/43_finance_closures.R` (the model) and `R/44_area_finance.R` (the area
pages); every number below is read from what they write.

One rule runs through all of it. **No open school is named.** A score is a
reason for a conversation about a school's future, not a forecast, and a
published list could help bring about the closures it describes. Scores for
individual schools are kept out of the published data; only counts by area
are shown.

## What is predicted {#sec-finance-method-outcome}

The unit is a **school-year**: one school's finance return for one year. For
school *s* in year *t*, the outcome is

$$y_{st} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if the last year the school taught is } t+1 \text{ or } t+2 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

so the model asks whether a school closes within the next two years, given
that year's return. A closure is a state mainstream school that GIAS records
as closed with no successor, or as merged into another school, as on
[Pupil numbers and school places](demographics.qmd#sec-demog-data). An
academy conversion, a change of trust or a change of type is not a closure:
the school carries on under a new number, and the two numbers are joined (see
[the data notes](finance.qmd#sec-fin-data)). Returns in or after a school's last
year are left out, since by then the closure is known.

The model years are `r FMm$years[1]` to `r FMm$years[2]`. They start in
2017-18 because the three-year change in pupils needs a return three years
earlier (the maintained-school returns begin in 2014-15), and they stop in
2023-24 so that every year has two full years of follow-up in GIAS.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fm-flow
#| tbl-cap: "How the model's sample narrows, from every finance return to the school-years the model is fitted on."
tibble(Step = c("Finance returns for state mainstream schools, 2014-15 to 2025-26, one a school-year",
                "Open that year (not in or after the last year taught), up to 2023-24",
                "At least 10 pupils and a positive income",
                "Every signal present (needs a return three years earlier, a capacity and an area trend)"),
       `School-years` = format(unname(FMm$flow), big.mark = ",")) |>
  kt(align = "lr")
```

That leaves `r format(FMm$n, big.mark = ",")` school-years from
`r format(FMm$schools, big.mark = ",")` schools, of which
`r FMm$events` were followed by closure within two years
(`r FMm$closing_schools` different schools, since a closing school can count
twice: two years out and one year out). Closure is rare: about
`r sprintf("%.1f", 1000 * FMm$events / FMm$n)` school-years in 1,000.

## The signals {#sec-finance-method-signals}

Each signal is read from the school's own return for that year, or from its
area. Percentages are capped, so a handful of odd returns (a school in its
first or last months, a return with almost no income) cannot steer the fit.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fm-signals
#| tbl-cap: "The signals in the model, how each is measured, and its spread across the model's school-years (one standard deviation, the unit of the effects below)."
fm_def <- c(log_pupils = "Pupils (full-time equivalent) on the return, logged",
            chg3 = "Change in pupils since the return three years earlier, %, capped at ±50",
            util_c = "Pupils as % of GIAS capacity, capped to 20-150",
            res = "Revenue reserve at year end as % of income, capped at ±40",
            iy = "Income less expenditure as % of income, capped at ±20",
            ipp = "Total income / pupils, logged",
            area_primary_chg = "The authority's change in primary-age pupils, 2018/19 to 2025/26, % (from the census)",
            academy = "Academy or free school, against maintained",
            secondary = "Secondary, middle-deemed-secondary or all-through, against primary")
fm_tab |> transmute(Signal = label, Measure = fm_def[term],
                    `One SD` = ifelse(per == "per SD", sprintf("%.2f", sd), "yes vs no")) |>
  kt(align = "llr")
```

Income per pupil is in cash terms and the model has no year term. Within a
year that changes nothing, since every school's funding moves together and
the ranking is left alone. Across years it does: cash rises lift every
school's income per pupil, and with it, a little, every later score.

## The model {#sec-finance-method-model}

A logistic regression:

$$\text{logit}\,\Pr(y_{st} = 1) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(\text{pupils})_{st} + \beta_2\,\text{chg3}_{st} + \beta_3\,\text{full}_{st} + \beta_4\,\text{reserve}_{st} + \beta_5\,\text{in-year}_{st} + \beta_6 \log(\text{income per pupil})_{st} + \beta_7\,\text{area}_{s} + \beta_8\,\text{academy}_{st} + \beta_9\,\text{secondary}_{s}$$

fitted by maximum likelihood on every school-year from `r FMm$years[1]` to
`r FMm$years[2]` for the published effects and scores, and on 2017-18 to
2020-21 alone for the test below.

```r
glm(y ~ log_pupils + chg3 + util_c + res + iy + ipp + area_primary_chg + academy + secondary,
    family = binomial, data = mm)
# `r format(FMm$n, big.mark = ",")` school-years, `r FMm$events` closing within two years
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-fm-effects
#| fig-cap: "Each signal's effect on the log-odds of closing within two years, per standard deviation (or yes against no), with 95% intervals; the top axis gives the same as an odds ratio. Left of zero, less likely to close."
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-width: 8.5
fe <- fm_tab |> mutate(label = factor(label, rev(label)), clear = lo_sd > 0 | hi_sd < 0)
ggplot(fe, aes(b_sd, label)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo_sd, xmax = hi_sd), colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = clear), colour = DPURPLE, size = 2.6, fill = "white", stroke = 1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ exp(.), name = "Odds ratio", breaks = c(0.2, 0.33, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3))) +
  labs(x = "Change in log-odds of closing within two years", y = NULL) + theme_note(11)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fm-coefs
#| tbl-cap: "The fitted model. The coefficient is per unit of the signal as measured (per percentage point, per log unit, or yes against no); the odds ratio is per standard deviation, as in the chart."
fm_tab |> transmute(Signal = label,
                    Coefficient = sprintf("%.4f", est), `Std. error` = sprintf("%.4f", se), z = sprintf("%.1f", zc),
                    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", or), `95% interval` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", lo, hi),
                    Per = ifelse(per == "per SD", "SD", "yes vs no")) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(Signal = "Intercept", Coefficient = sprintf("%.2f", fm_co$est[1]), `Std. error` = sprintf("%.2f", fm_co$se[1]),
                   z = sprintf("%.1f", fm_co$zc[1]), `Odds ratio` = "", `95% interval` = "", Per = "")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrl")
```

The model cuts the deviance from `r format(round(FMm$null_dev), big.mark = ",")`
(no signals) to `r format(round(FMm$dev), big.mark = ",")`, a McFadden
pseudo-R² of `r sprintf("%.2f", fm_r2)`; that is high for a rare event. How to
read three of the effects:

- **A falling roll is the strongest sign.** Each standard deviation of fall
  over three years (about `r round(fm_tab$sd[fm_tab$term == "chg3"])` percentage
  points) multiplies the odds of closing by
  `r sprintf("%.1f", 1 / fm_tab$or[fm_tab$term == "chg3"])`, with the school's size,
  fullness and money held fixed.
- **Academies close far less often** than maintained schools with the same
  figures (odds ratio `r sprintf("%.2f", fm_tab$or[fm_tab$term == "academy"])`).
  That is mostly how the system works: an academy in trouble is usually moved
  to another trust, which is not a closure, while a council closes a
  maintained school.
- **More income per pupil goes with more closure**, size for size. Funding
  follows last year's pupils and protects small schools, so a school whose
  roll is falling faster than its funding shows high income per pupil.

## How well it works {#sec-finance-method-test}

The test is out of time: the model is fitted on 2017-18 to 2020-21 (2016-17 has no three-year change in pupils, so adds no returns) and scores
the returns of 2021-22 to 2023-24, which it has not seen. The test years hold
`r format(FMt$n, big.mark = ",")` returns and `r FMt$closures` that were
followed by closure within two years.

**Ranking.** The area under the ROC curve (AUC) is the chance that a
randomly chosen closing school-year is scored above a randomly chosen open
one, computed from the ranks of the scores *p*:

$$\text{AUC} = \frac{\sum_{i: y_i = 1} r_i - n_1(n_1 + 1)/2}{n_1 n_0}$$

It is `r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$auc)` on the test years, with a 95% interval of
`r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$auc_ci[1])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$auc_ci[2])` from 500
bootstrap samples of schools (resampling whole schools, so a school's years
stay together). The riskiest 2% of test returns held
`r FMt$top2[["caught"]]` of the `r FMt$top2[["closures"]]` closures
(`r fm_pc(FMt$top2[["caught"]] / FMt$top2[["closures"]])`); the riskiest 5% held
`r fm_pc(FMt$top5[["caught"]] / FMt$top5[["closures"]])`.

**Earlier warning.** In the year before closure the decision may already be
known and parents leaving can be part of what the model sees. So a second
test leaves that year out and predicts closure two or three years on. Its
AUC is `r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$early$auc)`, and the riskiest 5% held
`r fm_pc(FMt$early$top5[["caught"]] / FMt$early$top5[["closures"]])` of
`r FMt$early$closures` closures. The warning is there well before the decision.

**Which signals carry it.** Refitting on one kind of signal at a time:
pupil numbers, fullness and the area trend alone give an AUC of
`r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$parts[["rolls"]])`; the finance measures alone
`r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$parts[["finance"]])`; maintained or academy alone
`r sprintf("%.2f", FMt$parts[["governance"]])`. Rolls and money each carry most
of the warning, and together do better than either.

**Calibration.** Ranking is not the same as getting the level right.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fm-calib
#| fig-cap: "Predicted and observed closure within two years in the test years, 2021-22 to 2023-24, for returns grouped by their score (the model fitted on 2017-18 to 2020-21). Log scale."
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| fig-width: 8
cb <- as_tibble(FMt$calib) |> pivot_longer(c(predicted, observed), names_to = "what", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(what = factor(what, c("observed", "predicted"), c("Observed", "Predicted")))
ggplot(cb, aes(pct, band)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = band), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = what, shape = what), size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Observed = DPURPLE, Predicted = BPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Observed = 19, Predicted = 17), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "% of returns followed by closure within two years", y = "Score band (test returns)") + theme_note(11)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fm-calib
#| tbl-cap: "The same, as numbers."
as_tibble(FMt$calib) |> transmute(`Score band` = band, Returns = format(returns, big.mark = ","), `Closing within two years` = closing,
                                  Predicted = sprintf("%.2f%%", predicted), Observed = sprintf("%.2f%%", observed)) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrr")
```

The bands are in the right order and the riskiest 2% are close
(`r sprintf("%.1f", FMt$calib$predicted[6])`% predicted,
`r sprintf("%.1f", FMt$calib$observed[6])`% observed), but the model fitted on
the earlier years predicts more closure than happened:
`r round(sum(FMt$calib$predicted * FMt$calib$returns) / 100)` closures in all
against `r FMt$closures`, with the gap widest, in proportion, in the low bands.
Closures were not rarer in the test years (`r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * FMt$base)`%
of returns, against `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * (FMm$events - FMt$closures) / (FMm$n - FMt$n))`%
in the training years). Rather, the same figures went with closure less often
than before, and cash rises in income per pupil may lift the later scores (see
above). This is why the site reports where a school stands
against others (a band, a count) rather than a probability for it.

## From scores to the published counts {#sec-finance-method-counts}

**Scores for open schools.** The model fitted on every year scores each open
school's latest return (2023-24 or later), where the school has at least 10
pupils and every signal.

**The band.** The highest-risk band is set from the model's own history: the
score above which the riskiest 2% of school-years from 2017-18 to 2023-24 fall,
a predicted `r sprintf("%.1f", fm_cut)`% chance of closing within two years. An
open school is in the band if its latest score is above that. Of
`r format(FM$now$schools, big.mark = ",")` open schools scored,
`r FM$now$flagged` (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * FM$now$flagged / FM$now$schools)`%) are.

**The warning signs.** Five plain readings of a school's own return, for
anyone without the model:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fm-signs
#| tbl-cap: "The five warning signs and their thresholds. A school's count is how many of the five it shows in its latest return."
tibble(Sign = c("Small", "Falling roll", "In-year deficit", "Reserve below zero", "Under capacity"),
       Threshold = c("Under 100 pupils (primary) or 600 (secondary)", "Pupils down 15% or more over three years",
                     "Spending more than income by over 3% of income", "Revenue reserve below zero at year end",
                     "Under 70% of GIAS capacity")) |> kt(align = "ll")
```

The thresholds are round numbers near where closing schools part from the
rest (see [the warning signs](finance.qmd#sec-signs)), not fitted values. A
primary school showing three of them closed within two years about
`r sprintf("%.0f", FM$sign_rates$rate[FM$sign_rates$stage == "Primary" & FM$sign_rates$n_signs == 3])`
times as often as one showing none.

**Counting.** The band and the three-or-more-signs counts are totalled by
authority in `R/43` and, for the Sussex districts, in `R/44`, which places
each school in a district by its location and recounts the signs from the same
list with the same thresholds. The two agree for Brighton and Hove, which is
both. The list of scored schools is written only to a private folder that is
never committed.

## The area finance pages {#sec-finance-method-areas}

The [area finance pages](finance_areas/brighton_and_hove.qmd) sum the same
returns by England, region, authority and Sussex district, for each year,
phase and sector. A school is in deficit when its revenue reserve is below
zero; shares and medians are of schools, totals and income per pupil are
sums over schools. Reserves are shown for maintained schools only, because an
academy in a trust reports only its share and many report none. Any share,
median or line needs at least five schools behind it. Authorities are ranked
among those with ten or more maintained schools; districts among the Sussex
districts with five or more.

## What the model does not do {#sec-finance-method-limits}

- **It is not causal.** It describes the schools that were closed, by the
  councils and trusts that closed them. A deficit does not close a school;
  a council deciding to does.
- **Its standard errors treat school-years as independent.** A school appears
  up to seven times, so the intervals on the effects are somewhat too narrow.
  The test AUC's interval does not have this problem: it resamples schools.
- **One model for both phases**, with a secondary term. Secondary closures
  are few (`r FM$n_closers$schools[FM$n_closers$stage == "Secondary"]` since
  2017-18 against `r FM$n_closers$schools[FM$n_closers$stage == "Primary"]`
  primary), too few to fit on their own.
- **No year or place terms** beyond the area's pupil trend. The rate of
  closure moves with policy and funding from year to year, which is why the
  levels are a little off in the test.
- **The area trend looks ahead.** It is one figure per authority, the change
  in primary-age pupils from 2018/19 to 2025/26, so for the early model years
  it holds some later information. Refitted without it, the test AUC is
  `r sprintf("%.3f", FMt$parts[["no_area"]])` against `r sprintf("%.3f", FMt$auc)`,
  so it adds little to the ranking; a strict forecast would still use the
  trend to date.
- **Capacity is GIAS's latest figure**, not the figure each year, and the two
  kinds of return run on different years (April to March, September to
  August).

See also [what this cannot tell you](finance.qmd#sec-fin-limits) on the
finance page.
